Thanks for the ping, Chloe — I reviewed the intake and their placeholder DPA (attached). High-level guidance below.

Short answer: send our Redwood DPA template via DocuSign and include the subprocessor attestation. We can accept limited customer redlines but will push back on any changes that materially increase risk (e.g., expanding data usage, broadening liability, or removing our right to subcontract).

Specifics:
- Cross-border transfers: Redwood uses the EU SCCs (processor-to-processor & controller-processor sequencing where applicable). We will include a Transfer Mechanism Schedule and option to add a Privacy Annex if they require additional controls.
- Subprocessors: provide current list in the envelope and a standard clause that customers will be notified of material changes 30 days in advance. We should not commit to bespoke carve-outs for every subprocessor.
- E-sign: DocuSign is fine. AdobeSign is supported but will add 24–48 hours to envelope prep in our workflows. If BrightBridge absolutely requires AdobeSign, note that in reply.
- Redlines: Acceptable redlines are limited to definitions and minor clarifications. Anything touching security obligations, termination, or indemnity goes to legal.
- Timeline: If we send our DocuSign envelope today (using Redwood_DPA_Template_Redlined.docx), and BrightBridge returns within 48 hours, we can sign and target enablement by 2027-03-24.

I attached a redlined version of our template with the clauses we expect to hold firm. If Ben needs to accelerate for sales, we can offer a one-time enablement credit but I’ll need exec approval for any SLA exceptions.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
